title: Smooth proper coherent trace pairings and their geometric naturality
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a smooth proper morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $\omega_Y=\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{Y/k}$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. For an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal E$ locally isomorphic on a Zariski open cover to $\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}$ for a finite integer $r$ (allowed to vary between components), put $\mathcal E^\vee=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(\mathcal E,\mathcal O_Y)$. Cohomology means right-derived global sections of Zariski module sheaves [pqf-def-cohomology], and cup product is the usual sheaf-cohomology product [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product]. There is a canonical $k$-linear map $t_Y:H^d(Y,\omega_Y)\to k$, the degree-zero map of the adjunction counit $R\Gamma(Y,f^!k)\to k$ under the smooth dualizing identification $f^!k\simeq\omega_Y[d]$; here $f^!$ is the right adjoint to $Rf_*$ on complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology, and $[d]$ is the cohomological shift. For every $0\leq i\leq d$, all the groups below are finite-dimensional and the pairing
$$P_{Y,\mathcal E,i}:H^i(Y,\mathcal E)\times H^{d-i}(Y,\mathcal E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y)\longrightarrow k,\qquad (u,v)\longmapsto t_Y(\operatorname{ev}_*(u\cup v))$$
is perfect: the induced maps from either factor to the linear dual of the other are bijective. Evaluation is $e\otimes(\lambda\otimes w)\mapsto\lambda(e)w$.
For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, put $Y_A=Y\times_k\operatorname{Spec}A$. The canonical maps $A\otimes_kH^j(Y,\mathcal F)\to H^j(Y_A,\mathcal F_A)$ are isomorphisms for $\mathcal F=\mathcal E,\mathcal E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y,\omega_Y$ and every $j\geq0$. There is a canonical trace $t_{Y_A}:H^d(Y_A,\omega_{Y_A/A})\to A$, equal to $1_A\otimes t_Y$ under these maps. The cup-evaluation pairings over $A$ are the scalar extensions of $P_{Y,\mathcal E,i}$. For any $A$-automorphism $h:Y_A\to Y_A$, the differential identification $h^*\omega_{Y_A/A}\simeq\omega_{Y_A/A}$ satisfies $t_{Y_A}(h^*z)=t_{Y_A}(z)$. If in addition $\eta:h^*\mathcal E_A\simeq\mathcal E_A$ is given, let $h_\eta^*$ act on cohomology by pullback followed by $\eta$, and let $h_{\eta^\vee}^*$ use the induced isomorphism on $\mathcal E_A^\vee\otimes\omega_{Y_A/A}$ (the dual of $\eta^{-1}$ and the differential on $\omega$). Then
$$P_{Y_A,\mathcal E_A,i}(h_\eta^*u,h_{\eta^\vee}^*v)=P_{Y_A,\mathcal E_A,i}(u,v).$$
These compatibilities respect composition of isomorphisms and of scalar extensions. The assertions include $d=0$, with $\omega_Y=\mathcal O_Y$.

source.place: Tag 0FVV, lemma-duality-proper-over-field (5),(7); Tag 0FVW, remark-duality-proper-over-field; Tag 0FVY, lemma-duality-proper-over-field-perfect; Tag 0FW0, remark-rework-duality-locally-free-CM; Tag 0B6J, lemma-trace-map-and-base-change; Tag 0AAB, lemma-proper-flat-base-change. Isomorphism naturality is the counit naturality with the canonical smooth differential normalization.

proof.text: Put $K_f=f^!k$ and write $\tau_f:R\Gamma K_f\to k[0]$ for the counit. Also use $K_p=p^!\mathcal O_S$ and $\tau_p$ for $p=f_A:Y_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, for any commutative $k$-algebra $A$, as well as for $p=f$. Smoothness supplies local finite presentation; properness supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness, so $p$ is of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] to obtain $K_p$ with its normalized polynomial-chart models and adjunction trace. Flatness for $f$ follows from [lem-pc-flat-field]; after base change it follows by tensoring the same flat algebra charts. The trace-pair characterization, uniqueness and arbitrary-base-change compatibility are those of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality], including its explicit agreement with Zariski proper duality when the spaces are schemes and the base affine. Thus no Noetherian hypothesis on an eventual $A$ is introduced.

source.place: Tags 0E4P, 0B6J; spaces-duality.tex Tags 0E61, 0E6C, 0E6E (proper dualizing pair and trace)

proof.text: Normalize $K_p$ by the differential line. Take the standard-smooth affine charts of [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension], of dimension $n-c=d$. Their closed immersions into polynomial affine space are immersions between smooth $S$-schemes. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-regular-immersion] locally, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] to their regular equations. The conormal description of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] then gives $[C\to V]\simeq L_{Z/S}$, with $V$ of rank $n$. Since $p$ is smooth this complex is $\Omega^1_{Z/S}[0]$; its differential cokernel is locally free of rank $d$ by [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], so locally this conormal sequence splits. It follows that $C$ has rank $n-d=c$. On these charts [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] identifies the normalized polynomial model of step 1 with $(\det C)^\vee\otimes\det V[d]$. The equality of ranks concerns these local charts, not a chosen global presentation.

source.place: Tag 0BV2 (local upper-shriek calculation), Tag 0BRT (smooth determinant calculation); divisors.tex Tag 067U

proof.text: By [lem-trf-lci-determinant-descent-smooth], the relation-first determinant map $(\det C)^\vee\otimes\det V\to\bigwedge^d\Omega^1_{Z/S}$ agrees with the intrinsic determinant and with its overlap maps. The polynomial comparisons in [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] use precisely these maps, including contraction of an extra relation $t-a$ with $d(t-a)$ to $1$. These local calculations imply that $K_p$ has cohomology only in degree $-d$. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] it is that cohomology sheaf shifted by $d$; the determinant maps identify this sheaf globally. Thus they give a specified $\kappa_p:K_p\simeq\omega_{Z/S}[d]$. Its isomorphism naturality can be checked using transported presentations: a family isomorphism takes the conormal map $[C\to V]$ to the transported map, hence on its cokernel it takes $db$ to $d(h^\sharp b)$. The induced map of determinant lines is exactly $\bigwedge^d dh$. Changing the chosen presentations changes neither map, by the cited refinement comparison. This identifies the action on the actual differential sheaf, rather than an arbitrary identification with a line.

source.place: Tag 0BRT; dualizing.tex Tag 0BZJ with the differential-form normalization; ordered Koszul and conormal determinant comparisons

proof.text: Set $t_Y=H^0(\tau_f\circ R\Gamma(\kappa_f^{-1}))$, using $H^0R\Gamma(\omega_Y[d])=H^d(Y,\omega_Y)$. The rank-$d$ statement [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] makes $\omega_Y$ a line (in a local basis its generator is the wedge of the $d$ basis vectors). In a local frame $\mathcal E\simeq\mathcal O^r$, the dual has the dual frame, and $\mathcal E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y$ is finite free of rank $r$. These sheaves are quasi-coherent and finitely presented by their local free presentations; $\mathcal E[0]$ is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Apply [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional] to each of $\mathcal E$, $\mathcal E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y$, and $\omega_Y$. This proves the required finiteness without connectedness or an algebraic-closure hypothesis.

For any complex $C$ of $k$-vector spaces, $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k)}(C[i],k[0])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^iC,k)$. Indeed $k$ is injective: extend a functional from a subspace by choosing a basis complement and setting it to zero there. Apply [new-stage3-derived-homology-injective-bijective] to $C[i]$; it says that this particular comparison is the map induced by cohomology, hence sends a derived morphism to its action on $H^0$. Apply it with $C=R\Gamma\mathcal E$. The adjunction characterization in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality], with the object $\mathcal E[i]$, identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(\mathcal E[i],K_f)$ with this vector-space dual. The map sends $a:\mathcal E[i]\to K_f$ to $\tau_f\circ R\Gamma a$, not to an unspecified linear equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0FVV (5) and its adjunction proof; injective-target cohomology comparison

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-perfect-rhom-tensor-comparison] for $\mathcal E[0]$ and $K_f=\omega_Y[d]$, and [lem-sfb-ringed-global-hom-cup-comparison] to identify the left side of step 5 with $H^{d-i}(Y,\mathcal E^\vee\otimes\omega_Y)$. The latter node also identifies the action of $R\Gamma a$ with cup followed by evaluation; [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product] identifies this with the stated module cup. Its order is the dual class followed by the $\mathcal E$ class. Interchanging the two total-complex cocycles multiplies by $(-1)^{i(d-i)}$, since the tensor symmetry on degrees $i,d-i$ is exactly that sign. Thus the transpose of the ordered pairing $P(u,v)$ differs, if required by this order convention, from the bijection of step 5 by multiplication by this unit sign. It is consequently bijective. Both spaces are finite dimensional by step 4, so the other transpose is also bijective: in bases its matrix is the transpose of an invertible square matrix. This proves perfectness for the pairing with the order and evaluation in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0FVY, 0FVB; perfect evaluation and global-Hom cup comparison

proof.text: Let $A$ be any commutative $k$-algebra. It is a flat $k$-module (choose a $k$-basis), so [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] applies, for every $j\geq0$, to the three quasi-coherent sheaves in step 4. Since $Y$ is separated and quasi-compact over $k$, its isomorphism is the specified canonical comparison of [lem-pc-flat-cohomology-separated], $\beta^j:A\otimes_kH^j(Y,\mathcal F)\to H^j(Y_A,\mathcal F_A)$, $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,p^*x$, and this map is bijective. By [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], the differential map is $b\otimes da\mapsto b\,d(1\otimes a)$; its top wedge identifies $(\omega_Y)_A$ with $\omega_{Y_A/A}$. Duals and tensor products of $\mathcal E$ commute with this pullback: in a frame the dual basis is carried to the dual basis and evaluation remains $\sum e_j\lambda_j$. Hence the three sheaves used in base change are precisely the sheaves occurring over $A$.

source.place: Tags 02KH and 0B6J; morphisms.tex, cartesian differential comparison

proof.text: The arbitrary-base-change trace-pair identification $\beta:Lp^*K_f\simeq K_{f_A}$ of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality] identifies $K_{f_A}$ and its counit with the pullback pair of $K_f$. To compare $\beta$ with the differential normalization, use the pulled-back charts of step 2: $B_A=B\otimes_kA$ with $P_A=P\otimes_kA$. Their relative dimensions remain $n-c=d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-base-change]. By [lem-sfb-proper-flat-polynomial-model-base-change], under the polynomial-chart comparisons on both sides, $\beta|_{U_A}$ is the coinduction base-change map $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(B,\Omega^n_{P/k})[n]\otimes_BB_A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_{P_A}(B_A,\Omega^n_{P_A/A})[n]$. That node imposes no Noetherian hypothesis on $A$. The cotangent comparisons of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] commute with this flat, hence Tor-independent, base change. The dual Koszul comparison of [lem-trf-lci-koszul-duality-determinant-comparison] for the pulled-back equations is obtained by the same contractions after tensoring. The base change is flat, so the free Koszul resolutions remain resolutions, and a contraction of the ordered top relation with its dual is $1$ before and after tensoring. Hence on $H^{-d}$ the map $\kappa_{f_A}\circ\beta\circ p^*\kappa_f^{-1}$ is the determinant of the conormal and differential base-change maps, that is, the top wedge of the differential base-change map of step 7. Taking $H^0R\Gamma$ of the trace-pair equality, with the comparison $\beta^d$ of step 7, proves $t_{Y_A}=1_A\otimes t_Y$. This uses flatness over $k$, not Noetherianity of $A$.

source.place: Tags 0B6J, 0AAB and 0E2Y; dualizing.tex Tag 0E2F (arbitrary base change of the polynomial model); differential-form normalization and flat Koszul extension

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-space-derived-cup-base-change] to the square $Y_A\to Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the two vector-bundle complexes and their evaluation coefficient map. Together with [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product] and step 7, its equality says on pure tensors that the cup-evaluation class of $a\otimes u,b\otimes v$ is $ab\otimes\operatorname{ev}_*(u\cup v)$. After step 8 its trace is $ab\,t_Y(\operatorname{ev}_*(u\cup v))$. Pure tensors generate both scalar extensions, so the pairing over $A$ is exactly $A\otimes_kP$.

source.place: Tag 0H99 (derived relative cup/base-change square), followed by Tag 0B6J

proof.text: Let $h:Y_A\to Y_A$ be an $A$-isomorphism. Pull the dualizing trace pair back by $h$. For each derived quasi-coherent $M$, its represented Hom functor is unchanged: $\operatorname{Hom}(M,h^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}((h^{-1})^*M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\Gamma((h^{-1})^*M),A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\Gamma M,A)$. The last isomorphism is the canonical identification of global sections under an isomorphism, with inverse the one induced by $h^{-1}$. Thus uniqueness of the trace pair in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality] supplies its trace-preserving comparison. This is the intrinsic comparison on the polynomial models of [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model]. Step 3 computes it, using transported charts, as $\bigwedge^d dh$ on $\omega$. Consequently its degree-zero counit equation is $t_{Y_A}(h^*z)=t_{Y_A}(z)$. This argument is over $A$ itself and allows $h$ which does not descend to $k$.

source.place: Trace-pair uniqueness (spaces-duality.tex Tag 0E5Z); Tag 0BV2 and differential determinant normalization

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-space-derived-cup-base-change] with $g=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$, $g'=h$, $f=f_A=f'$, and the coefficient maps induced by $\eta$ and its specified dual. This is a commutative square, which need not be presented as a Cartesian square. On local sections $e,\lambda,w$ the coefficient identity is
$$((\eta^{-1})^*\lambda)(\eta e)\,dh(w)=\lambda(e)\,dh(w).$$
Hence cup-evaluation of the transformed classes is $h^*$ of the original evaluated class. Step 10 removes this pullback after applying the trace. This proves the displayed invariance of $P$ with the dual of $\eta^{-1}$, including its inverse in exactly the required position.

source.place: Tag 0H99 with coefficient naturality; trace-preserving family-isomorphism comparison

proof.text: Composition requires no new choices: trace-pair comparisons compose because both composites induce the same functional on every test object, so uniqueness in [lem-sfb-proper-flat-space-derived-duality] identifies them. The intrinsic cotangent comparisons in [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] respect compositions, and their determinant maps do too by the cocycle of [lem-trf-lci-determinant-descent-smooth]. At the cochain level the base-change map sends $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s_A$; for $A\to B$ its composite sends $b\otimes(a\otimes s)$ to $ba\,s_B$, the direct map. Thus steps 7--11 respect composition of scalar extensions and isomorphisms. If $d=0$ the exterior power is the empty wedge $\mathcal O$, with the same normalized contractions and all signs equal to $1$. Empty schemes or rank-zero bundles give zero cohomology spaces and the unique maps; their zero pairings induce the unique isomorphisms $0\simeq0$. The proof applies componentwise with no connectedness assumption.
